reviewer: Kimi actually viewed the exact 65x67 original and its independently enlarged source-note derivative, the complete unchanged 2048x2048 external-06 raw PNG, the native-resolution note crop at x=1030,y=900,width=820,height=600, and the full white/cyan/source-alpha/return-alpha comparison. Checked the two note rows, irregular group shapes, right-edge tab, brows, cap, clothing, collar, frame, alpha, and the task/prompt/request/result bindings before approving this exact output SHA.

hair_features.reason: The cap retains its two principal silver-toned insignia groups, braid and glossy visor. Dark brows remain visible beneath the visor; the chin is smooth with no added moustache, beard or glasses. Covered hair areas were not replaced with invented exposed hair.

collar_fit.reason: The field-gray high collar and two pale rectangular collar tabs fit around the compact rounded chin and short broad neck transition. The dark central opening remains coherent without a pinched narrow collar, floating cloth, long yellow neck column or cream bib.

entries.positive_observation: The note now has TWO separated irregular gray-mark groups in EACH of its two rows, including the restored lower-right group, rather than the rejected uniform long bars. The small dark right-edge tab and blank lower paper remain. The capped yellow mascot has dark brows, one restrained mouth and the source-compatible viewer-right pose; the cap, dark tunic, fitted collar, dark photographic frame/backplate and directional lighting are retained without an extra person or replacement scene.
entries.alpha_decision: Native RGBA is 2048x2048 with extrema 0..254. Counts are 0=1528895, 252=1199064, 253=1262282, 254=649 and 255=0. The actual white/cyan/alpha views show intact photographic backing, clothing, note and exterior without visible interior holes or a working-matte halo. Internal alpha 252-254 is accepted under the current visible-alpha policy; no alpha-only repair is claimed or needed.
entries.visible_limitations: The exact tiny cap/collar insignia and note glyphs cannot be resolved at 65x67. Approval is based on the visible source-compatible groups, irregular shapes, clothing and composition, using the independently enlarged original note for comparison; it does not claim reconstruction of readable text or microscopic heraldry.
